edetect.warranty_note: The threshold is not backtested or tuned: for ANY pre-change distribution in the calibrated class, thresholding an e-detector at 1/alpha yields E[N*] >= 1/alpha — a nonasymptotic Frequentist average-run-length guarantee (arXiv:2203.03532, Thm. 2.4), valid at every sample size with no asymptotic regime and no multiple-comparison penalty for continuous monitoring. The warranty prices false alarms; it says nothing about the cause of a true one.

caveats: the pre-change class is calibrated on the FIRST 40 days only (mean bound padded 3 se, scale inflated 1.5x, plus a per-component |lam|*sigma/2 margin): the ARL warranty is exact INSIDE that calibrated class — under Gaussian baseline noise the padding fails only for a >3-sigma calibration draw (~0.3% per side) or a >33% scale underestimate (~1% at n=40), and heavier-than-Gaussian pre-change tails can void it entirely; the guarantee is exactly as good as this calibration
sensitivity is the price of the warranty: shifts below ~0.5 sigma-hat accrue evidence too slowly to alarm quickly — this tripwire rules on regime breaks, it does not scan for drifts
two independent detectors run (spread + tail); by the union bound the SYSTEM-level warranty halves to 1 false alarm per 500 days in expectation
after each alarm the accumulator restarts from zero: the FIRST alarm of a run carries the clean warranty; subsequent alarms are conditional statements about further changes
increments are clipped at ±12 sigma-hat so one corrupted print cannot manufacture evidence or overflow the accumulator

edetect.method: Shin–Ramdas–Rinaldo e-detector (arXiv:2203.03532), sub-Gaussian instantiation, per stream. Pre-change class calibrated on the first 40 obs: mean bound mu0 +/- 3 se, scale sigma_hat = 1.5x baseline sd. Baseline increments L_n(k) = exp(lam_k*(X_n - mu_k)/sigma_hat - lam_k^2/2) on the FIXED a-priori grid lam in [-2.0, -1.0, -0.5, -0.25, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0] (K=8, uniform mixture — Prop. 2.3), each component's null boundary mu_k = mu0 +/- (pad + |lam| sigma_hat/2) so validity is exact inside the class (E[L] <= exp(-lam^2/2)). Each component runs Shiryaev–Roberts M_n = L_n*(M_{n-1} + 1), the sum of e-processes restarted at consecutive times. Alarm when the mixture reaches 1/alpha = 1000 (Thm. 2.4: E[N*] >= 1/alpha = 1000 days, nonasymptotic). Change-date = argmax restart index of the dominant component's e-process at the alarm. Expected delay for a shift of D sigma-hat: ~ (ln(1/alpha) + ln K) / max_lam(lam*D - lam^2/2) days. Accumulator restarts from zero after each alarm.

caesar.method: pop = SOFR−IORB − trailing 5bd median (imported from backtest.pop_bp, THE shared event statistic; n=2077bd), modeled in negated space y = −pop. CAESar AS-(1,1) per arXiv:2407.06619 (Gatta–Lillo–Mazzarisi) — CAViaR (Engle–Manganelli 2004) extended to a joint (VaR, ES) estimator: [q; e]_t = [b0; g0] + [b1 b2; g1 g2]·[(y+); (y−)]{t−1} + [b3 b4; g3 g4]·[q; e]{t−1}. Three steps: (1) CAViaR quantile regression as an exact Koenker–Bassett LP (linprog/HiGHS, persistence bounded to [0, 0.999]) in a fixed point over the recursion's lag, multi-started from three deterministic anchors on cold refits; (2) ES−VaR gap autoregression under the BCGNS squared-excess loss with soft monotonicity penalty; (3) joint Nelder–Mead re-estimation of the Fissler–Ziegel / Patton–Ziegel–Chen loss with penalties for e > q and q > 0 (lambda=10); published pairs monotonicity-repaired. Expanding-window walk-forward from a 500bd prefix, refit every 5bd with coefficients carried between refits; one-step-ahead forecasts scored under the same FZ loss against rolling-250bd climatology (order-statistic quantile, tail-mean ES). Verdict self-demotes to climatology when the loss ratio >= 1.

gyre.method: resid = spread − rolling 30bd median (Undertow's residual family), scaled by EXPANDING MAD (min 120 obs, trailing) → x. Simplex projection: k=E+1 nearest library neighbors, library = vectors whose h-step future resolved strictly before t with Theiler exclusion |s−t| ≥ E+h (min 300 vectors), weights exp(−d/d_min). Decay: Pearson rho and MAE-vs-persistence per h in (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21) over post-warmup targets. Determinism gate: 20 phase-randomized surrogates (rfft phases scrambled, DC/Nyquist kept, seed 7) preserve the linear autocorrelation exactly; actual rho must clear their 95th percentile (targets subsampled every 3, same subsample for the actual). S-map: locally weighted linear regression over the full library, weights exp(−theta·d/d̄), theta in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 8.0), lstsq on the weighted design (every 5th target); state dependence = rho_best − rho(0) > 0.03. Stability: the S-map coefficients at theta 2 form the top row of an E×E companion matrix; largest |eigenvalue| = local expansion multiplier, read as an expanding percentile vs its own past. cases.subject: Seiche itself: the PROOF scoreboard and the composite

rows.evidence: Expanding window discipline is enforced by unit test: test_history_has_no_look_ahead appends future data and requires every already computed index value to stay identical, and the same invariant is pinned on undertow, tidetables, swell and bathymetry. The Leak Audit then rebuilds the same index with the two dominant leak classes deliberately switched on (full sample standardization, a centered smoother) and publishes the Leakage Gain each break would buy.

Nothing in the composite is fitted, so there is no training set to disclose: the weights and the alert percentile are frozen in config.py and PROOF prints its warmup slice and its caveat list. The gap: those editorial choices were made by an operator who had already seen the full history, and no document separates the data that shaped the design from the data that now grades it. Disclosed, but not separated.

The genuinely held out sample is the live record since first publication: the PIT ledger commits one record per day per stream, and the attest layer signs each committed record (Ed25519) and anchors it to Bitcoin through OpenTimestamps, so a post publication reading is sealed before its outcome. The backtest window itself is not held out: the design saw it. The true out of sample record is the attested one, and it is still short.

Every input is a registered SeriesSpec in config.py with mnemonic, source ID, fetch start and native lag. The funding event is defined once (backtest.pop_bp: SOFR minus IORB against its trailing 5 business day median, 10bp threshold) and every consumer imports that definition. Registry tests pin fetch starts so a retune cannot silently starve an engine.

The whole pipeline is public AGPL-3.0 code; the board snapshot is baked to frontend/public/data/overview.json on every publish; the Time Machine endpoint (/api/asof/{date}) replays the full light board as of any historical date; and the PROOF scoreboard has its own signed and Bitcoin anchored stream (attest prove-scoreboard).

PROOF consumes final vintage values: the FRED collector reads fredgraph.csv, which serves the current revised history, and no ALFRED as published replay exists in this codebase. The PROOF page prints the caveat (weekly H.4.1 aggregates are lightly revised; daily market prints effectively are not) and the PIT ledger accrues true as published readings from publication day forward, but the historical backtest itself rides revised values. That is the gap, named.

Editorial, frozen, disclosed: the alert percentile (80) and the composite weights sit in config.py under a TUNING POINT banner that calls them the tool's editorial voice, and nothing in the pipeline refits them. The Leak Audit's THRESH_FIT row publishes what an in sample fitted threshold would have bought, and PROOF's AUROC is threshold free, so the cost of the editorial choice is measured. But measured is not derived: the numbers come from judgment, not from a walk forward derivation, and this rubric does not round that up.

Published readings are append only: the notary hash chains every reading so editing any past day breaks every link after it, and the attest layer makes a rewrite attributable (signature) and undatable (Bitcoin anchor). rows.evidence: The claims ship with no stated look ahead protections. Rebuilt with them (trailing median signal, no look ahead), the public layer's 6 month spread is +0.0167 with a 95 percent interval of [-0.0320, +0.0647].
No design or evaluation split ships with the claims: no error bars, no out of sample tests, no design sample named. The referee page states that absence above the fold.

Nothing is held out because nothing is released to hold out. The referee's own held out test on the public layer refuses to certify the asset price lead; at the claimed 13 month business cycle lead the correlation reads +0.15 in [-0.14, +0.46], n 257.

The largest agreed component is public and is reconstructed here: G3 central bank assets at monthly average spot, 282 months from 2003-01-31 to 2026-06-30. The remaining layers, private credit and cross border flows across some 80 countries back to 1974, are defined in prose and reproducible by nobody outside the firm.
The index is proprietary: no series, no code, no error distribution. The referee page commits to rerunning every test the day an error distribution is released.

No revision record ships with the claims, so as published values cannot even be distinguished from today's history. An index family whose vintages are unpublished is ungradeable on this row, and ungradeable by choice is a FAIL, not an N/A.

The claimed windows, 3 to 6 months, 12 to 15 months and a 65 month cycle, arrive with no stated derivation. Tested on the public layer, the business cycle correlation peaks at a 22 month lead. The sample's spectral resolution at 65 months is plus or minus 15.6 months: too coarse to certify the cycle either way.

The claims are undated and carry no changelog and no stated policy for revising or retiring a claim that fails. A claim that cannot fail in public is copy, not a forecast; the referee page's dated changelog is what the alternative looks like.

rubric.method: Adapted from the coded execution assumption matrix of arXiv:2606.08285. Grades are PASS, PARTIAL, FAIL or NOT_APPLICABLE, N/A only with a stated reason, and every row carries evidence a reader can check. The self grade is built from repo facts (unit tests by name, config constants, the attested PIT ledger); the external case is populated from what engines/refereegli.py actually established, with live numbers when the block is lit.
